data.title: SpeakON Connects Voice Notes and AI Agent Tasks to Move Everyday Ideas Forward
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Useful ideas often come without any warning. A person could be mowing the grass, getting work done at the office, or dropping off kids at work and suddenly have a clear goal or motivation that needs addressing. The thought may be clear, but taking the time to type it, organize it, and act on it isn’t always possible.

Image: Man records a voice note on his iPhone with an orange SpeakON device outdoors.

SpeakON is developing a new way to capture every little detail. While users are already getting comfortable with an AI voice button for iPhone as a starting point, SpeakON Notes preserves context so the SpeakON Agent can organize supported follow-up work. That is beyond the capabilities of a simplified AI chatbot. Users don’t only transcribe an idea into words, but turn meaningful direction into action, without sacrificing control over what is sent or changed.

Capture the Thought Without Rebuilding It Later

The SpeakON hardware button and compatible iPhone software let users speak any idea whenever it strikes. Using an active text field, SpeakON transforms natural speech patterns into fully editable text, creating an independent note.

These AI voice notes for iPhone retain more than a fragmented idea. Notes preserve the “substance” of information. It allows context to be built around a new observation, meeting follow-up, or instruction.

Inside SpeakON, users can manage multiple different Notes in the same grouping, merge related Notes after previewing recommended combinations, and revisit a Weekly Summary that organizes information, activity, and underlying ideas with links to those Notes. That is a lot of time-saving capability without hands-on intervention.

If a user is more acclimated to Notion, Evernote, or local Obsidian vaults, SpeakON Notes can sync reviewed contacts. That bridges the gap between captured information and knowledge systems the user already knows.

Image: SpeakON AI voice notes turn a spoken client follow-up into an editable note on iPhone.

From a Note to a Coordinated Follow-Up

SpeakON Notes are just the beginning. A manager leaving a client meeting with tons of activities to manage can press on SpeakON to “Update the group with the latest rollout dates in Slack, draft an email to Leah with any new revisions due Friday, and remind me to follow up on Monday.”

The SpeakON Agent delivers that context. It can recognize what the user wants completed, create a new Task, and use supported context to prepare any future steps or actions. For example, it can search Slack for relevant information, match the recipient in Contacts, prepare a draft email in Mail, and then set a reminder.

This ability to take information into action is the difference between Notes and Agent. Notes keeps all the original context. Agent uses that context to coordinate supported Actions.

Image: SpeakON syncs AI voice notes from its Notes app to Notion, Evernote, or Obsidian.

Make Captured Knowledge Useful Again

SpeakON is changing the AI industry by relating data to context over a longer period. Many modern LLM agents lose context the deeper the chat goes. That means a researcher recording observations after several customer touchpoints may miss details needed for future market research or company growth.

With SpeakON, each recording becomes an editable Note. The researcher could review the content, automatically sync it with Notes in Notion, and then divide tasks to team members. Earlier Notion onboarding can then be compared with today’s interviews and summarized with changes.

SpeakON supports many additional connections and apps including Notion, Slack, Google services, and eligible Evernote accounts. With Google, that means Gmail, Calendar, Contacts, and Drive. It even supports native iPhone actions, including Calendar events, Reminders, Contacts, and Mail draft creation.

Image: SpeakON Agent turns a saved note into a draft Slack team update for user confirmation.

The User Decides What Moves Forward

SpeakON is a user-centric innovation. It may be positioned in the market as a voice-first AI assistant, but it offers much more. While not fully autonomous, any Task can send or change data, but the user controls it by confirming the action to ensure continuity and digital safety. That review boundary ensures no next step begins without first getting permission.

The difference in capabilities is why SpeakON is more of an AI Communicator. It is a dedicated voice entry point paired with software that preserves context and completes supported goals. It’s inspired by the idea of speaking into a single device rather than communicating across multiple screens.

Image: SpeakON compares interview notes with a Notion onboarding guide to highlight conflicting feedback.

What Is Available Now, and What Comes Next

SpeakON’s focus on voice capture, independent Notes, bulk note management, syncing, Task creation, and supported third-party actions supports streamlined work and context preservation. New features are being onboarded as live availability and platform scope develop. That could include voice notes with daily summaries and voice-to-checklist capabilities.

Image: SpeakON summarizes daily AI voice notes and converts follow-up items into a checklist.

Given how many people need to capture ideas between meetings or update family members while running errands, SpeakON offers a streamlined solution that connects ideas to actions in a way other AI agents cannot quite manage. Wrapped into a single button on an iPhone, it lets users complete real tasks with retained context for their natural spoken ideas.

The latest iPhone-compatible voice button, Notes, and Agent capabilities help reduce information loss during the busiest moments of personal and business activities. data.description:
07:58 AM EST, 11/19/2026 (MT Newswires) -- US equity futures were higher pre-bell Thursday as traders geared up for the market debut of Claude AI chatbot creator Anthropic (ANT).

Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were 0.6% higher, S&P 500 futures were up 1.2%, and Nasdaq futures were 2% lower.

Anthropic plans to raise $81.3 billion in what is considered to be the largest stock-market debut, with the start of trading due following Thursday's market open. The company priced its IPO of 980 million Class A shares at $83 apiece after previously planning to offer 825 million shares between $70 and $78 apiece.

Traders also assessed the latest round of earnings. Walmart ( WMT ) posted higher fiscal Q3 adjusted earnings and revenue, while Alibaba Group ( BABA ) reported higher fiscal Q2 non-GAAP earnings and revenue.

Oil prices were higher, with front-month global benchmark North Sea Brent crude up 0.9% at $92.77 per barrel and US West Texas Intermediate crude 0.9% higher at $83.07 per barrel.

Initial jobless claims, scheduled for release at 8:30 am ET, are projected to have decreased to 198,000 in the week ended Nov. 14 from 200,000 in the previous week, according to estimates compiled by Bloomberg. The Philadelphia Fed's regional manufacturing index for November is seen coming in at 20.1, down from 20.9 posted previously.

data.title: C-Suite airline leaders estimate disruption costs an airline $5-10 million a year, according to new IBS Software research
data.description:
ATLANTA, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The annual cost of disruption for an airline was estimated at between $5 million and $10 million, according to 54% of C-suite respondents in new research from IBS Software. Disruption can affect operational costs, compensation, rebooking, customer support and customer loyalty.

The research of 500 airline leaders (including 259 holding C-Suite roles) found 2 in 3 (66%) rank their airline as well prepared to manage large scale disruption, with 67% of leaders saying the wider industry is also well prepared.

This is at odds with the passenger perspective, with only 26% of 2000 UK and US consumers surveyed agreeing that the airline industry is well prepared to manage large scale disruption events. That presents a large confidence gap and a disconnect that communication alone cannot address.

Getting ahead of disruption is critical for improved customer satisfaction

Just 1% of airline leaders say they can notify passengers instantly (0% in the UK and 2% in the USA). 10% have the ability to notify within 1–15 minutes, while 45% need 16–30 minutes to communicate with travellers when a disruption occurs.

Passengers are feeling the effect of this communication delay, with slow notifications impacting their attitude towards disruption. Yet, despite the majority of airline leaders reporting they are well prepared to handle delays, lack of updates rank among the biggest disruption frustrations for 29% of consumers, and 34% say timely, clear updates matter most when plans change.

For nearly 2 in 3 consumers overall (63%) proactive communication would improve their opinion of an airline, with the inability to communicate in real-time potentially impacting return bookings for airlines.

Julian Fish, Head of Aviation Operations at IBS Software commented on the research, "As the holiday season approaches, airlines should prepare not just to handle disruption, but to keep passengers informed as soon as it becomes apparent. Technology must identify upcoming issues, and then connect operational systems with passenger communications, allowing airlines to turn changing flight schedules into timely updates and rebooking options. Legacy technology infrastructure should not stand in the way of a faster, more coordinated response. The priority is giving passengers clarity about what happens next in the case of a delay, with accessible support and rebooking options when they need it."

Support and ancillary services lag behind

Airline leaders are recognising where passengers feel the strain. They name long customer-support waits as the leading frustration (40%), followed by personalised support (30%) (rebooking and support shaped around the passenger's own journey) and clarity on compensation (29%).

When it comes to the secondary, ancillary services that surround a journey, only 26% of airline leaders with such access sold and serviced through their airline say they can automatically amend or rebook lounge access during disruption, and less than 1 in 5 (17%) say they can do the same for hotel bookings.

To learn more about IBS Software's approach to optimising airline operations, visit here.

Methodology

The research was conducted by Censuswide, among a sample of 2,000 UK and US consumers (1,000 per market) and 500 UK and US airline leaders (manager-level+ professionals) (250 per market). The data was collected between 12.10.2026 - 20.10.2026. Censuswide is a member of the Market Research Society (MRS) and the British Polling Council (BPC), and a signatory of the Global Data Quality Pledge. Censuswide adheres to the MRS Code of Conduct and ESOMAR principles.

About IBS Software

IBS Software is a leading travel technology company delivering AI-native travel intelligence that enables smarter, faster and more resilient decision-making, with built-in guardrails across aviation, cargo and logistics, and leisure and hospitality. It powers core capabilities for leading travel brands worldwide, spanning airline retailing, passenger services, loyalty, fleet, hub and crew operations, cargo management, and cloud-native platforms for hotels and cruise line operators, and operates from 17 offices globally.

* Dollar edges down but still near highest since April 2, 2025

* Yen falls against dollar, euro after safe-haven rally

* Hawkish Fed signals keep further rate hikes on investors' radar

By Stefano Rebaudo

Nov 19 (Reuters) - The dollar index edged lower on Thursday, ending a seven-session positive streak, as investors paused ahead of Anthropic's market debut, which is seen as a key test of appetite for riskier assets and broader market sentiment.

The dollar rally started on November 10 when hotter-than-expected US inflation data bolstered expectations that the US Federal Reserve would tighten its policy.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller called for a more aggressive response to inflation, while minutes of the central bank's October 27 to 28 meeting showed policymakers increasingly concerned that additional tightening might be needed.

Nasdaq futures rose more than 2% on Thursday after Anthropic priced its IPO above the marketed range, bolstering expectations for a strong debut and reviving sentiment around AI stocks.

The dollar index this week reached its highest level since April 2, 2025, when US President Donald Trump revealed a sweeping tariff package, triggering a selloff in US assets.

It was last down 0.05% at 103.77, after reaching 103.97. The euro rose 0.12% to $1.0989.

Barclays analysts said fiscal stimulus and strong AI-related capital spending point to a resilient US economy, a wider output gap and higher-for-longer interest rates, all supportive of dollar strength.

The dollar's gains have come despite a selloff in technology shares.

"First, the market has also repriced a more hawkish Fed given recent commentary pushing the interest rate differential wider, but the dollar seems to be overshooting this move," said George Saravelos, global head of forex strategy at Deutsche Bank, explaining the recent rise.

"Second, and more intriguingly, foreigners have been very aggressive buyers of US equities even as the stock market has tumbled," he added.

A Deutsche Bank tracker following more than 100 foreign-domiciled exchange-traded funds showed large dip-buying of US stocks by foreigners over the last two weeks, the biggest buying spree so far this year.

Such a move reinforces the view that the dollar has been supported by investor flows into US equities.

YEN SLIPS AS SAFE-HAVEN FLOWS FADE

The dollar was up 0.35% to 159.90 yen, snapping a four-day losing streak.

Analysts said that a further selloff in AI-linked assets could support the yen through safe-haven buying and repatriation flows, with the impact likely to be more pronounced against other currencies than against the dollar.

According to Barclays estimates, a 10% decline in the S&P 500 from its peak could push dollar/yen towards 155, while a 20% decline could pressure it towards 152.

The euro was up 0.50% versus the Japanese currency at 175.73, after falling about 1.5% since late last week.

The Aussie dropped about 1% to $0.67 after hitting a fresh 11-month low. Australia's employment fell for a second straight month in October and the jobless rate climbed to a five-year high, bolstering the view that rates have likely peaked.

"The sharp hawkish repricing of Fed rate hike expectations is contributing (to) the weakness in commodity prices and related currencies," said Lee Hardman, senior currency analyst at MUFG.

UBS brought forward its forecast for the first Reserve Bank of Australia rate cut to August next year from November, and extended the easing cycle to three cuts from two, citing elevated inflation and a deterioration in the labour and housing markets.

data.title: Fed policymakers concerned about financial system risks, minutes show
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Financial stability risks tied to aggressive artificial intelligence investment and elevated asset prices are on the US central bank's radar, the minutes from the Federal Reserve's policy meeting last month showed on Wednesday.

The concern was raised as part of a broad review of financial risks by Fed policymakers and central bank staff at the October 27-28 policy meeting. That gathering saw officials hold interest rates steady despite ongoing worries about high and persistent levels of inflation. However, "almost all" policymakers agreed that further hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes showed. 

"The staff judged that current vulnerabilities could amplify shocks somewhat more than usual, with elevated asset valuations and leverage at hedge funds representing the most salient vulnerabilities, while strong bank and household balance sheets provided an important buffer against more severe outcomes," the minutes said.

Policymakers expressed concern that huge levels of investment in AI technology could lead to trouble and create broader problems for both the financial system and economy.

"Almost all participants commented on risks associated with a scenario in which the returns on AI investment turned out to be disappointing to investors," the minutes said. "Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures," while "a few" of the unnamed Fed officials were concerned that AI exposure was being concentrated in a "small number" of companies.

Fed officials also cast an anxious eye toward hedge funds.

"Most participants highlighted hedge fund leverage or limited dealer intermediation capacity as potential channels of amplification during periods of market stress," the minutes said.

Fed staff described the financial system as "resilient," with banks having ample access to cash, according to the minutes. But some policymakers worried that "banking system vulnerabilities could emerge rapidly even after seemingly reassuring initial assessments."

Some were also worried the Fed's data on the banking system may miss the full range of exposure some financial firms have.

BUILDING RESILIENCE

Financial markets have been under stress in recent weeks amid questions about the future of AI and how the buildout of the technology has increasingly come to rely on debt. Past periods of financial trouble have been frequently associated with excessive borrowing, and some of those crises have driven the Fed to intervene to stabilize markets.

The latest minutes also showed Fed officials weighing how they can respond to future troubles.

"A few" policymakers mulled boosting banks' capital levels while some also said it is important to better prepare banks to use the Fed's emergency lending discount window facility, which is something officials have been working on for some time.

In addition, "a few" policymakers considered a novel strategy in which the Fed would set up a dedicated method of asset-buying that would explicitly target financial stability concerns.

The Fed is weighing the future of how it uses its balance sheet as a policy tool. Fed holdings have swollen massively over the last two decades due to huge bond purchases during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.

The pandemic experience has loomed particularly large because bond-buying that began in March 2020 started out as a stabilization tool that morphed into outright stimulus.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack is among those who would like to see a more clearly defined system for buying bonds that would also entail a strategy to sell them when a crisis has passed. Hammack said earlier this week that any program "should also be temporary, and holdings should be sold in a timely way once market financial stability is restored." 

The minutes noted that "several" policymakers cautioned that monetary policy is not the right tool to deal with market trouble. But the large role now played by AI and technology investment in driving economic growth might complicate that view if large-scale problems emerged.

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: TSMC tightens China AI chip curbs as new US rules close manufacturing loophole, sources say
data.description:
* Chinese designers face suspension of previously permitted advanced chipmaking orders

* TSMC guidance generally limits affected customers to older 28nm and 40nm technology

* Restrictions threaten China's efforts to develop alternatives to Nvidia's ( NVDA ) AI chips

By Che Pan and Wen-Yee Lee

Nov 19 (Reuters) - Taiwan's TSMC is tightening restrictions on Chinese chip designers, suspending some previously permitted advanced manufacturing orders and generally limiting affected customers to older chipmaking technology, according to two people familiar with the matter.

The move could close one of the last remaining routes for Chinese companies to produce powerful AI processors, complicating Beijing's efforts to develop domestic alternatives to chips designed by Nvidia ( NVDA ) and manufactured by TSMC.

The world's largest contract chipmaker has instructed that affected orders using manufacturing processes of 16 nanometres and below be halted unless customers obtain US export licences, the people said.

Chinese designers will generally be limited to older 28-nanometre and 40-nanometre processes, provided their chips do not use high-bandwidth memory (HBM) or require advanced packaging, according to TSMC guidance reviewed by the two people.

Most leading AI chips are produced using 7-nanometre processes or smaller, enabling faster and more energy-efficient performance. HBM allows processors to handle the vast data volumes required by AI applications, while advanced packaging integrates chips and memory to boost computing power.

US CLOSES MANUFACTURING ROUTE

The restrictions follow new US Commerce Department rules that took effect on Thursday, removing a compliance route that had allowed some Chinese designers to access advanced manufacturing services without individual export licences.

Previously, TSMC could check the computing power and other technical characteristics of certain Chinese chip designs to determine whether they fell outside US export controls.

Under the new rules, TSMC can no longer use that verification process for affected Chinese customers. Their advanced chips are instead presumed to be covered by US controls, requiring export licences unless an exception applies.

The Financial Times first reported on Thursday that TSMC and South Korea's Samsung Electronics ( SSNLF ) had suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers following the new restrictions.

CHINA'S AI CHIP AMBITIONS

The measures could particularly affect Chinese companies developing alternatives to Nvidia's ( NVDA ) processors, including independent chip designers and technology giants that have developed in-house chips.

A US government list of approved chip designers includes Nvidia ( NVDA ), AMD, Apple ( AAPL ) and Taiwanese companies MediaTek and Realtek, but no mainland Chinese firms.

Some Chinese AI chip designers still had access to TSMC's 7-nanometre manufacturing technology before Thursday, a separate source with direct knowledge of the matter said. Reuters could not independently verify the arrangements under which those chips were manufactured.

data.title: Almost All Fed Officials See Need For Additional Rate Hikes, October Minutes Show
data.description:
03:29 PM EST, 11/18/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Almost all Federal Reserve officials agreed that interest rates must rise further to cool inflation, minutes from the central bank's October meeting showed Wednesday.

In a split vote on Oct. 28, the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee held its policy rate steady after a 25-basis-point hike in September. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack preferred another quarter-percentage-point hike last month.

"Almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate -- broadly consistent with the September Summary of Economic Projections -- would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2% objective," the minutes showed.

A couple of participants at the October meeting said the Fed may need to raise its policy rate by more than 25 basis points at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable, according to the minutes.

US inflation has remained above the Fed's 2% target for nearly six years. Most participants at the October FOMC meeting viewed price pressures to be broad based and expected inflation to remain elevated in the near term, the minutes showed.

"Many participants viewed the (artificial intelligence) buildout as a material source of inflation risk," according to the minutes.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC Wednesday that the central bank may need to lift interest rates aggressively because inflation was "headed in the wrong direction."

The minutes showed a "stronger conviction in further hikes than (Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's post-meeting) press conference conveyed, with disagreement mainly over timing, a message we have received from Fed speakers since this meeting," said Vikram Rai, senior economist at TD Economics.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said Wednesday that raising interest rates will be appropriate to bring inflation down to the 2% target in a timely manner, joining other central bank officials who have recently leaned hawkish.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday that the FOMC will likely need to lift its policy rate "several" times before spring. Hammack has also pushed for policy tightening, though she recently said that it must be undertaken gradually.

Markets widely expect the central bank to raise its benchmark lending rate by 25 basis points next month, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

"A 25-basis-point December increase looks consistent with the broad consensus, but it is not assured, and a larger move is a conditional minority view," TD Economics' Rai said. "Broader inflation pass-through could require more restriction, while weaker AI investment and improving supply could limit it."

data.title: Walmart nudges up annual forecasts ahead of crucial holiday season
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Walmart ( WMT ) slightly raised its annual targets on Thursday, betting that demand for lower-priced groceries and growth in its delivery business will support sales during the holiday shopping season.

The muted outlook from the world's largest retailer, a key barometer for the health of the American consumer, showed that shoppers continue to focus their spend on groceries and other essentials, while seeking value for other discretionary items.

The retailer now expects fiscal 2027 net sales to grow 4.9% to 5.2%, compared with its previous forecast of 4% to 5%. Analysts on average expect growth of 5.5%, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Walmart ( WMT ) forecasts annual adjusted earnings per share of $2.84 to $2.89, up from its previous range of $2.80 to $2.87. Analysts expected annual profit per share of $2.88.

The company has cut prices on thousands of grocery and general merchandise items this year as Americans seek cheaper options amid steep inflation and record-high gas prices.

US retail sales rose only moderately in October as higher prices squeezed consumer spending, forcing lower- and middle-income households to prioritize essentials and defer big-ticket purchases such as furniture.

Walmart's ( WMT ) push into faster delivery has helped drive repeat purchases, while customers using the service were also more likely to sign up for its membership program, the company said in August.

Rival Target reported another strong quarter on Wednesday and raised its annual forecast as investments in merchandise under new CEO Michael Fiddelke began to pay off.

Walmart ( WMT ), whose CEO John Furner took over earlier this year, has also focused on higher-margin categories such as fashion and invested in private-label brands, seeking to attract shoppers with lower-priced apparel and home decor.

The retailer has posted mixed results and remained cautious about its outlook this year as persistent inflation, higher gas prices and geopolitical uncertainty weighed on consumers.

Freight and logistics costs have also surged following the US war on Iran, squeezing profits across industries, including consumer goods and retail.

Operating expenses jumped 5% to $40.01 billion in the reported quarter, while total revenue rose by a better-than-expected 5.2% to $188.84 billion.

The company launched a cheaper bundled Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus membership in October ahead of the holiday shopping season.

Walmart ( WMT ) has increasingly relied on its membership, advertising and marketplace businesses to support margins while keeping prices low for value-conscious shoppers. Membership fee revenue rose by double digits in the three months through October.

(Reporting by Juveria Tabassum in Bengaluru and Nicholas P. Brown in New York; Editing by Anil D'Silva)

data.title: METALS-Copper bounces from 7-month low, eyes on strong China demand
data.description:
(Recasts, adds comment and London dateline)

By Pratima Desai

LONDON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Copper prices bounced on Thursday from a seven-month low hit the previous day as bargain hunters entered the fray and the market focused on demand from top consumer China, where stocks of the metal have dropped to three-year lows.

Benchmark copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 0.7% at $12,558 a metric ton at 1138 GMT. That is a drop of 16% since the record high of $14,875 a ton touched in September, partly due to fears that AI-related demand may not be as strong as had previously been expected.

The selloff was exacerbated by copper's slide through key support levels, which triggered further selling by funds that use algorithms and technical signals for trading, traders said.

Chinese demand for copper is expected to be a dominant theme. This is seen in the Yangshan copper premium , a gauge of China's appetite for importing the metal, hitting a record high at $360 a ton.

Stocks in warehouses monitored by the Shanghai Futures Exchange , at three-year lows of 27,642 tons, are down 94% since March due to traders and producers shipping copper to the United States ahead of potential tariffs on imports.

"What began as an American effort to secure supply may now encourage others to do likewise," said George Griffiths, head of markets at AMT Futures.

"The resulting scarcity is not necessarily evidence of an absolute shortage of copper, but rather a growing reluctance among those holding it to release it."

Griffiths expects this reluctance will provide a floor for copper prices.

Meanwhile, worries about aluminium supplies on the LME have pushed the premium for the cash over the three-month forward to 38-year highs of $256.50 a ton.

Aluminium stocks are at 36-year lows.

Three-month aluminium was up 0.7% at $2,843 a ton, zinc climbed 1.6% to $3,540, lead slipped 0.3% to $1,860, tin fell 1.6% to $42,125 and nickel retreated 1.2% to $15,660.

Overall, a strong US currency due to expectations of higher US interest rates is likely to weigh on dollar-priced metals.

(Reporting by Pratima Desai; editing by Joyjeet Das)

data.title: France's OVHcloud launches AI cloud products hosted in Europe
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - OVHcloud has launched 55 cloud-computing and AI products that run on infrastructure hosted in Europe, including access to Nvidia's ( NVDA ) latest AI chips and a workplace application combining email, documents and videoconferencing with AI assistants, it said on Thursday.

European governments and companies increasingly scrutinise where AI services are operated and how their data is handled, creating opportunities for regional providers seeking to compete with US cloud and AI firms.

The French cloud provider said its data centres, which have 110 megawatts of free capacity, could take up to 60,000 of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) new Blackwell chips, which it said matched the largest global platforms.

For the past three years, OVHcloud has lacked the chips and reserved them for existing customers rather than using them to win new ones, CEO Octave Klaba said at the company's summit held in the Louvre museum in Paris.

The new services will be available on the state-certified cloud that already hosts the French government's electronic invoicing platform, the system at the centre of a nationwide reform in force since September, OVHcloud said.

Emmanuel Spina, head of state agency AIFE, told the summit the reform would spare businesses lost invoices and bring automated bill processing.

OVHcloud also announced partnerships with cloud-computing company Shadow, Qwant and EUSP, a joint venture between Qwant and Ecosia that develops a European search index.

Qwant's AI-generated summaries are already powered by OVHcloud's Olala model and hosted in European data centres, handling up to 3 million queries a day and cutting the search engine's computing costs to a third of what they used to be, the companies said.

data.title: Balance Theory Acquires VectorBlack to Advance AI-Native Cybersecurity Decision Intelligence
data.description:
Acquisition expands cybersecurity investment intelligence and brings experienced industry leadership to Balance Theory

COLUMBIA, Md.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Balance Theory, the AI-native platform for cybersecurity investment decisions and execution, today announced the acquisition of VectorBlack, an AI-powered decision intelligence platform that will bring a new dimension of market visibility, competitive insights, and technology performance intelligence to cybersecurity leaders.

This acquisition comes on the heels of Balance Theory’s $19 million Series A financing announced in July 2026, which has supported the company’s mission to bring incident-grade discipline to how chief information security officers (CISOs) make cybersecurity investment decisions.

VectorBlack was developed to proactively equip CISOs with timely, relevant decision support on emerging cybersecurity threats, industry developments, and trends. By anticipating the issues likely to capture the attention of CEOs, boards, and business leaders, VectorBlack helps CISOs stay ahead of the news cycle, initiate informed conversations, and provide valuable context before questions arise—strengthening their credibility and influence as trusted strategic advisors.

Rather than simply aggregating information, VectorBlack is designed to help security leaders understand what has changed in the cybersecurity landscape, why it matters to their organization, and what actions deserve attention. The technology originated with co-founder Jason Lewis, who began developing the underlying product before joining forces with industry analyst Gerry Eaton and cybersecurity entrepreneur Wayne Schepens. Together, the founders evolved the concept into a platform focused on the needs of enterprise security leaders.

As part of the transaction, Schepens will join Balance Theory as Chief Cyber Market Analyst, bringing his cybersecurity industry expertise to help shape market strategy and product adoption. Lewis will serve as Principal Data Engineer, leading the continued development and integration of VectorBlack's technology, while Eaton will focus on applying the platform to deliver targeted research, market insights, and sector-specific intelligence to cybersecurity leaders.

VectorBlack's focus as a CISO Strategic Intelligence Platform was shaped by input from leading security executives, including Ryan Clarque, CISO at Black Rifle Coffee, who helped identify the need to connect timely market intelligence with the investment decisions and business priorities facing security leaders.

“CISOs need to understand what's changing in the market, what it means for their security programs, and where they should be focusing their investments,” said Ryan Clarque.

“An emerging technology, a shift in a vendor's strategy, or a new security challenge will influence our priorities. Real value comes from connecting that intelligence to the context within our organizations. We need capabilities to pull in the context of where we've already invested, our gaps, and what's delivering the outcomes we want. Having that strategic viewpoint before a renewal, budget decision, or board discussion can make all the difference.

“As we adapt to the new pace of AI-driven risks, the need for more informed cybersecurity decision-making has never been more imperative. VectorBlack and Balance Theory together will be the trailblazer for the kind of advanced capability CISOs and boards will depend on. This combination will enable the confidence to execute at the speed of threats,” Clarque concluded.

“Balance Theory gives CISOs greater visibility and control over their technology investments, from evaluating security solutions and measuring an average 300%+ first-year ROI to managing renewals and understanding which decisions deliver results,” said Greg Baker, Co-Founder and CEO of Balance Theory. “VectorBlack will take Balance Theory’s capabilities a step further by delivering tailored intelligence across the security product categories our customers invest in. This creates a powerful new level of insight to inform smarter technology investments and long-term security strategy.”

Balance Theory will integrate VectorBlack’s technology into its platform, adding to the proprietary market intelligence that already informs its customers’ investment decisions. By monitoring market developments, competitive dynamics, emerging technologies, and real-world experiences with security solutions, the combined teams will help CISOs understand not only how their own investments are performing, but what others in the industry are seeing, which approaches are delivering results, and where the market is headed.

“Building VectorBlack gave us the opportunity to rethink how cybersecurity information can be transformed into decision-ready intelligence,” said Lewis. “We're excited to continue that work at Balance Theory and build on what we've already developed.”

Details regarding future product integration and availability will be announced by Balance Theory.

About Balance Theory

Balance Theory is an AI-native platform for cybersecurity investment decisions and execution. The company was founded on a simple belief: cybersecurity leaders deserve a company built to help them make better decisions, not simply buy more. With the CISO as its north star, Balance Theory combines persistent program context, proprietary market intelligence and AI agents to help security teams manage more than $1 billion in cybersecurity investment spend, with customers averaging over 300% first-year ROI. Learn more at https://balancetheory.io/.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: EMERGING MARKETS-AI jitters knock EM stocks to 7-month lows, battered rand awaits rate decision
data.description:
* Anthropic IPO tests durability of AI trade

* Senegal budget setback clouds IMF programme

* Rand near 1-year low ahead of SARB rate decision

By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

Nov 19 (Reuters) - Emerging market stocks fell to fresh 7-month lows on Thursday, as AI jitters hammered some tech-heavy Asian markets, while currencies took a breather with the South African rand edging up from one-year lows ahead of an interest rate decision.

The MSCI emerging market equities index fell 1%, on course to record its first six-day losing streak since July 2024. Stocks in Taiwan plunged 4.4%, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng index fell nearly 2% on concerns about AI financing after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO.

However, stock markets in emerging Europe such as Poland's WIG20 and Hungary's Budapest SE index climbed, helped by a relatively low exposure to technology companies.

Global investors are keenly awaiting Anthropic's market debut later in the day after the AI startup raised $81 billion that valued the Claude chatbot maker at $1.5 trillion.

"There has also been speculation that foreign interest in Anthropic's blockbuster IPO has seen some demand for the dollar this week," said Chris Turner, global head of markets research at ING.

"If that is the case, that dollar demand could wane into tomorrow once IPO allocations are settled."

The US dollar index edged down after a seven-session winning streak fuelled by hawkish remarks from a Federal Reserve official that reinforced the case for further rate hikes.

A retreat in the dollar supported several commodity-linked currencies after sharp declines in recent days.

The South African rand edged higher after touching a one-year low of 17.36 per dollar earlier in the session, pressured by weaker precious-metal prices and uncertainty over coalition talks.

Investors are awaiting the South African Reserve Bank's (SARB) policy decision later in the day, and economists broadly expect the bank to keep rates unchanged following a hike at its previous meeting. However, recent data showed a surge in consumer inflation in October.

"No one is expecting a further hike today. However, money markets do price another 25bp hike in early 2027... the SARB has been responsive to the inflation shock and we see much greater scope for the rand to bounce back," ING's Turner said.

Most other currencies were rangebound as markets awaited trade and geopolitical signals from a closely watched trilateral summit between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia.​‌

Ahead of the summit, US President Donald Trump told his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping that they should both help end the war in Ukraine.

SENEGAL FISCAL IMPASSE IN FOCUS

Senegal's president has decided to implement the revised 2026 budget bill by decree, his office said, as an impasse continued with parliament that threatens to derail a new support programme from the International Monetary Fund.

The bill is key to advancing the IMF programme, which underpins the West African country's strategy to rework its massive debt burden.

In Poland, consumer sentiment weakened slightly in November as households assessed their current financial situation more negatively, while expectations for the coming year improved modestly, data from the statistical office showed.

Investors also monitored developments in the Middle East conflict.

Brent crude edged up after losses in the prior session as expectations for a market surplus outweighed lingering worries about Middle East supply amid attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Iran-aligned Houthi movement fired missiles at the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh, but the Saudi Civil Defense agency said the danger had passed.

(Reporting by Tharuniyaa Lakshmi in Bengaluru; Editing by Shailesh Kuber)

The blue-chip FTSE 100 fell 0.3% to 10,522.96 points as of 1111 GMT. The midcap FTSE 250 index ticked down 0.1% to 24,328.34, set for its sixth consecutive session of declines.

* UK stocks lagged a tech-led rally in Europe, with optimism around Anthropic's market debut doing little to buoy the domestic market

* "(If) investors become more enthused with tech, non-tech indices like the FTSE 100 will come under stress, which could lead to further losses if the post-Anthropic optimism is sustained," Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, said

* Defensive corners of the market were the main drag: Among consumer staples Unilever ( UL ) fell 2.1%, and British American Tobacco ( BTI ) dropped 1.7%; National Grid dropped 2.5% and AstraZeneca ( AZN ) lost 1.1%

* Limiting declines, industrial metal miners rose 1.1% to recover from their biggest one-day decline since April 4 in the previous session, as copper prices rebounded nearly 0.8%

* Anglo American, Antofagasta ( ANFGF ) and Glencore ( GLCNF ) rose more than 1%

data.title: Morning Bid: ANTics
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic finally goes live on Thursday after the AI debutante's IPO was priced at $83 per share, well above earlier guidance, bumping up the overall valuation to $1.5 trillion. That makes the IPO the biggest on record in terms of the value of shares sold.

But even though demand has clearly been brisk, the eventual value is still some 25% below indications from only a few months ago. That speaks to the shakeout in the wider market that's taken place since early October. And it remains tense.

Even though positive soundings on Anthropic's mega IPO helped the Nasdaq inch back up on Wednesday, troubled Nvidia fell again despite its earnings beat on Tuesday. The S&P 500 also clocked its fifth consecutive daily drop, putting the week's losses at well over 3%.

Asia's tech stocks tumbled again initially overnight, with the big APEC summit in Shenzhen looking more like a photo op than a meeting of substance that could tackle the tense tech trade issues between Washington and Beijing. There was a late rally in those markets, however, and Nasdaq futures are up about 2% before Anthropic's debut.

The other big worry across markets is the increasingly hawkish drumbeat from Fed officials about getting inflation back to target. Fed minutes from the October meeting showed that most policymakers were pushing for more hikes, with some considering a larger 50 basis point rise as the next move.

One of those, governor Christopher Waller, doubled down on his push for a 50 bps hike on Wednesday, saying the Fed needed to get "aggressive" and shock people to ensure that today's 3% inflation rate would not be considered the norm.

That's a difficult market for Anthropic to start trading in, and the rest of the US economy also has reason to worry about credit tightening. We'll get more insight on the current strength of the consumer when Walmart reports later today.

The dollar continues to feed off the contrast between aggressive Fed tightening expectations and less hawkish forecasts for other major central banks, nudging to a new 19-month high overnight.

Finally, the European Union summit on Friday will also be watched closely on a range of issues. This could include the reveal of the new European Central Bank chief, who is almost certain to be former Bank of Spain Governor and current Bank for International Settlements boss Pablo Hernandez de Cos. Compared with other potentially more hawkish names mentioned in recent months, he would be considered more of a consensus figure and thus unlikely to change current ECB thinking in a major way.

CHART OF THE DAY

Anthropic's IPO will be the biggest ever in terms of the value of shares being listed when it debuts on Thursday.

However, the overall valuation of the company at $1.5 trillion is still shy of SpaceX's $1.75 trillion tally when it listed in June. It's also 25% below where Anthropic's valuation was being guided only two months ago.

-- Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson, Fed board governor Michael Barr, Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin, Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack all speak; European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde speaks

data.title: India's gamers skip work, crowd cafes for Grand Theft Auto VI as Modi joins buzz
data.description:
* India has an estimated 550 million gamers, mostly mobile

* Console-only release sends fans to cafes offering hourly packages

* PM Modi posts GTA-styled graphics comparing India in 2013 with today

* Top YouTubers' 10-hour streams draw over 13 million views each

By Munsif Vengattil, Bhawika Chhabra and Sharafat Ali

BENGALURU, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Jacob Joel first played Grand Theft Auto in school, then again in college. On Thursday, the 30-year-old IT professional took the day off to play GTA VI in a Bengaluru gaming cafe's mini-theater, steering a speedboat beneath a bridge on a 100-inch projection screen with surround sound.

"We waited around 13 long years to get into GTA VI ... that is a nostalgic feeling," Joel said, controller in hand, eyes fixed on the screen.

Made for an estimated $1 billion or more, "Grand Theft Auto VI" launched worldwide on Thursday to glowing early reviews, in what is billed as the most anticipated video game release in history.

In India, one of the world's largest gaming markets with an estimated 550 million players and where most gaming happens on mobile phones, the launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI" turned a console-only title into a social event. It sent players to gaming cafes, drove hours-long live streams and even drew in Prime Minister Narendra Modi, underscoring the growing appeal of premium gaming as a cultural marker.

Popular Indian gaming YouTubers CarryMinati and Mythpat each streamed GTA VI for about 10 hours, drawing more than 13 million views apiece by Thursday afternoon.

"India is playing a whole new game!" Modi wrote on X, above 10 images modelled on Grand Theft Auto artwork that compared India at the time of GTA V's 2013 release with the country today.

Modi has stepped up efforts to woo young voters since youth-led protests over jobs and education pushed his party to sharpen its social media outreach.

CAFES FILL CONSOLE GAP

Reuters spoke to at least a dozen gamers who crowded gaming cafes in cities including Delhi, Bengaluru and Srinagar on launch day.

Because GTA VI is available only on consoles, gaming cafes offered many Indian players a cheaper alternative to buying the hardware. The cafes charge as little as 250 rupees ($2.67) per hour.

At the Gaming Mania cafe in Delhi, players sank into tan couches with white controllers, as one complained to another that he had not yet spotted a single bike in the game.

Divya Gupta, 48, co-owner of the cafe, said that she had fielded 40 to 50 calls through the day, including from small children asking whether they could play. She said GTA slots were fully pre-booked through Sunday despite a slight price increase.

In Bengaluru, Navin Rajendran, 50, owner of the Gamineazy cafe, said the rush was about more than just playing the game.

"This is something people want to be seen playing. It's about the bragging rights," he said.

(Reporting by Munsif Vengattil in Bengaluru, Bhawika Chhabra in New Delhi and Sharafat Ali in Srinagar; Editing by Xevi Fontdegloria)

data.title: US STOCKS-Nasdaq futures climb on optimism ahead of Anthropic's market debut
data.description:
* Futures up: Dow 0.67%, S&P 500 1.25%, Nasdaq 2.15%

* Anthropic IPO pricing lifts AI-linked stocks

* Cybersecurity firms up after Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) lifts FY27 forecast

(Updates prices throughout, adds analyst comments)

By Medha Singh and Utkarsh Hathi

Nov 19 (Reuters) - Nasdaq futures rose more than 2% on Thursday after Anthropic priced its IPO above the marketed range, bolstering expectations for a strong debut and reviving sentiment around beaten-down AI stocks.

Anthropic priced its upsized offering at $83 per share, above its $70 to $78 range, raising $81 billion in the largest listing on record that valued the AI lab at about $1.5 trillion. It will begin trading on the Nasdaq later in the day.

The listing follows weeks of selling in chipmakers and cloud companies, as investors fretted over stretched valuations, hefty spending on AI infrastructure and the fallout from Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt exit.

"A strong debut is the tonic that the market needs after such a volatile period... it tells us that investor demand is still there," said Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX.

"We can't underestimate the importance of this IPO. It sort of serves as a valuation for the wider AI ecosystem."

Hyperscalers Amazon and Alphabet, also among the investors in the AI startup, added 2.2% and 3.9%, respectively, in premarket trading.

Chipmakers also gained, with Nvidia ( NVDA ) up 1.8% after falling for five straight sessions through Wednesday, as upbeat revenue forecast did little to uplift sentiment.

Intel ( INTC ), Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), Micron , and Marvell ( MRVL ) rose between 3.2% and 4.6%.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius gained 4.8% each, while data center-related companies IREN ( IREN ) and Applied Digital ( APLD ) climbed 5.4% each.

At 05:48 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 335 points, or 0.67%, S&P 500 E-minis were up 92 points, or 1.25%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 585.5 points, or 2.15%.

The S&P 500 logged its fifth consecutive session of decline on Wednesday, with Hawkish minutes from the US Federal Reserve's latest meeting also weighing on sentiment.

Nearly all Fed officials saw a need for more rate increases if the economy performed as projected, according to the minutes from the central bank's October policy meeting, while a few warned that inflation could be stickier than anticipated and could call for tighter policy.

Investors will now parse remarks from several Fed officials due later on Thursday.

Traders are pricing in near-certainty of a 25-basis-point hike at the Fed's December meeting and about an 8% chance of a 50-basis-point move, according to LSEG data.

Among other movers, Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) shares jumped 10% after the cybersecurity firm raised its 2027 revenue forecast, helping drive gains of 4.5% to 7% in peers CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) , Cloudflare ( NET ), Okta ( OKTA ) and Zscaler ( ZS ).

Walmart ( WMT ) is scheduled to report quarterly earnings before the opening bell on Thursday.

(Reporting by Medha Singh, Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur in Bengaluru; Editing by Ronojoy Mazumdar and Shilpi Majumdar)

data.title: Maximus Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year Results for Fiscal Year 2026
data.description:
Completes Agile Defense acquisition, delivers earnings above guidance, and establishes fiscal year 2027 guidance

TYSONS, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Maximus ( MMS ) , a leading provider of government services, reported financial results for the three months and year ended September 30, 2026. The acquisition of Agile Defense, LLC (Agile Defense) was completed on November 18, 2026.

Highlights for fiscal year 2026 include:

  • Full year revenue of $5.23 billion, landing within the guidance range.
  • Full year operating margin of 11.7% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.2%, along with diluted earnings per share of $7.27 and adjusted diluted earnings per share of $8.24, which exceeded the top end of guidance and increased 12.0% over the prior year on an adjusted earnings per share basis.
  • Full year cash flows from operating activities of $112 million and free cash flow of $69 million. Subsequent to fiscal year-end, collections totaled more than $330 million from a major customer.
  • Repurchases of Maximus ( MMS ) common stock totaling approximately $192 million during fiscal year 2026.
  • Establishes fiscal year 2027 guidance of $5.45 billion to $5.65 billion of revenue, adjusted diluted earnings per share of $7.50 to $8.00, and free cash flow of $700 million to $800 million; fiscal year 2027 guidance reflects the absence of an estimated $1.05 per share of benefit recognized in fiscal year 2026 attributable to a specific program, which is discussed further below.
  • A quarterly cash dividend of $0.33 per share payable on November 30, 2026, to shareholders of record on November 13, 2026.

"Fiscal year 2026 reflected the benefits of disciplined execution, technology-enabled productivity enhancements, and thoughtful capital allocation," said Bruce Caswell, President and Chief Executive Officer. "Throughout the year, we continued deploying automation and AI-enabled solutions across our operations, improving efficiency, strengthening profitability, and delivering meaningful outcomes for customers. These efforts contributed to adjusted diluted earnings per share of $8.24, representing 12.0% growth over the prior year and performance above the top end of our most recently updated guidance range."

Caswell continued, "Subsequent to fiscal year-end, we completed the acquisition of Agile Defense, which significantly expands our position in defense and national security markets and enhances our portfolio of technology-enabled capabilities. As we enter fiscal year 2027, we remain focused on integrating Agile Defense, growing existing customer relationships, executing on opportunities associated with recent policy initiatives, and further advancing our leadership in AI-enabled solutions and technology innovation."

Agile Defense Acquisition Close

On November 18, 2026, Maximus ( MMS ) completed its acquisition of Agile Defense, a provider of mission-focused technology solutions supporting customers across the Department of War, Intelligence Community, homeland security, and civilian agencies.

The acquisition expands Maximus' ( MMS ) presence in defense and national security markets while adding differentiated capabilities in cybersecurity, digital modernization, software and analytics, cloud solutions, and AI-enabled mission support services. The transaction further diversifies the U.S. Federal Service's portfolio, enhances access to strategically important customers, and increases exposure to attractive markets with favorable long-term growth characteristics.

Agile Defense is expected to contribute approximately ten months of revenue during fiscal year 2027 and is included in the fiscal year 2027 guidance.

Consolidated Fiscal Year 2026 Results

Revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $5.23 billion, compared to $5.43 billion reported for the prior fiscal year. As previously discussed, fiscal year 2025 benefited from elevated natural disaster support activities and temporary clinical program volume surges that did not recur at the same level during fiscal year 2026. Revenue finished within the fiscal year 2026 guidance range and was consistent with our expectations throughout the year.

For fiscal year 2026, the operating margin was 11.7% and adjusted EBITDA margin was 14.2%, compared to 9.7% and 12.9%, respectively, in the prior fiscal year. The improvement reflects technology-enabled productivity enhancements, including automation initiatives, disciplined cost management efforts, and strong operational performance.

Diluted earnings per share were $7.27 and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $8.24 for fiscal year 2026. This compares to $5.51 and $7.36, respectively, in the prior fiscal year. Adjusted diluted earnings per share exceeded the top end of the most recently updated guidance range for fiscal year 2026 and increased 12.0% over the prior year. Earnings growth was driven principally by improved operating performance reflected in the margin improvement and the benefit of capital deployment actions, including share repurchases.

U.S. Federal Services Segment

U.S. Federal Services Segment revenue for fiscal year 2026 was approximately $2.99 billion. Prior fiscal year revenue of $3.07 billion benefited from nearly $100 million of elevated natural disaster support activity and temporary clinical volume surges that did not recur at the same level during fiscal year 2026.

The segment operating margin for fiscal year 2026 was 18.1%, compared to 15.3% reported for the prior fiscal year. Margin expansion was driven by technology-enabled efficiencies, productivity improvements, strong execution across core program areas, and favorable operating leverage generated through automation initiatives deployed throughout the fiscal year. Together, these factors helped create opportunities to efficiently process higher volumes and improve profitability, such as incentive payments on the Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Disability Examination (VA MDE) program during the first three quarters of the fiscal year 2026.

Fourth quarter results of fiscal year 2026 reflected the previously disclosed customer-directed modification to the VA MDE program regarding performance incentives. The fourth quarter also benefited from strong performance across the clinical portfolio, which is expected to moderate in fiscal year 2027.

U.S. Services Segment

U.S. Services Segment revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $1.68 billion, compared to $1.76 billion reported for the prior fiscal year. Revenue performance was generally consistent with expectations and reflected varying volumes across several contract areas. Revenue trends improved throughout fiscal year 2026, culminating in positive organic growth in the fourth quarter.

The segment operating margin for fiscal year 2026 was 9.1%, compared to 9.7% reported in the prior fiscal year. Fiscal year 2026 results included a $6.9 million non-cash impairment charge related to a software asset developed and capitalized for a specific customer.

We continue to see encouraging demand indicators associated with Medicaid community engagement requirements, program integrity activities, eligibility administration, and other state government initiatives that are expected to support future growth opportunities.

Outside the U.S. Segment

Outside the U.S. Segment revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $557 million, compared to $600 million reported for the prior fiscal year. The revenue decrease was attributable to previously divested businesses as well as lower revenue across several employment services and clinical programs amidst certain customer-specific challenges.

The segment reported a modest operating loss, primarily reflecting the lower revenue across those employment services and clinical programs. Maximus ( MMS ) continues to focus on driving profitable growth through disciplined bid selection, operational improvements, and successful conversion of its sales pipeline.

Sales and Pipeline

Signed contract awards for fiscal year 2026 totaled $2.51 billion, and contracts pending (awarded but unsigned) totaled $1.86 billion at September 30, 2026. The book-to-bill ratio at September 30, 2026, was 0.5x on a trailing twelve-month basis and the quarterly book-to-bill ratio improved to approximately 1.0x, representing the strongest quarterly award performance of fiscal year 2026.

The fourth quarter book-to-bill ratio was enabled by a signed contract award for a significant state Medicaid contract renewal representing more than $800 million of total contract value over a ten-year period. Included in the contracts pending balance are two recently awarded state Medicaid contract renewals totaling approximately $528 million of total contract value.

The total sales pipeline at September 30, 2026, was $44.8 billion (comprised of approximately $4.01 billion in proposals pending, $1.61 billion in proposals in preparation, and $39.2 billion in opportunities tracking). New work opportunities represent approximately 61% of the total sales pipeline, and U.S. Federal Services Segment opportunities represent approximately 58% of the total sales pipeline.

During fiscal year 2026, Maximus ( MMS ) achieved a recompete win rate of approximately 89%, reflecting the strength of its customer relationships, operational performance, and technology-enabled service delivery model.

Balance Sheet and Cash Flows

At September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $280 million, and gross debt was $1.61 billion. The ratio of debt, net of allowed cash, to consolidated EBITDA for the full year ended September 30, 2026, as calculated in accordance with our credit agreement, was 1.8x.

Following the completion of the Agile Defense acquisition, our pro forma leverage ratio is expected to be approximately 2.3x, remaining within Maximus' ( MMS ) targeted leverage range of 2x to 3x and preserving financial flexibility for future capital allocation priorities.

For fiscal year 2026, cash flows from operating activities totaled $112 million and free cash flow was $69 million, enabled by $278 million of free cash flow for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. This compares to $429 million and $366 million, respectively, in the prior fiscal year.

Days sales outstanding, or DSO, were 93 days at September 30, 2026, compared to 98 days at June 30, 2026. Subsequent to fiscal year-end and through November 13, 2026, we collected more than $330 million from a major customer that had been anticipated in our fiscal year 2026 guidance. As a result, a portion of cash generation expected during fiscal year 2026 shifted into fiscal year 2027 guidance due to timing-related factors rather than collection concerns. During fiscal year 2026, we repurchased approximately 2.6 million shares of Maximus ( MMS ) common stock totaling approximately $192 million. As of November 13, 2026, the full $400 million balance from the most recent Board of Directors authorization remains available.

On October 5, 2026, our Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.33 for each share of our common stock outstanding. The dividend is payable on November 30, 2026, to shareholders of record on November 13, 2026.

Fiscal Year 2027 Guidance

Maximus ( MMS ) is establishing fiscal year 2027 guidance.

We expect revenue to range between $5.45 billion and $5.65 billion. The outlook includes approximately ten months of contribution from Agile Defense and reflects expectations for continued growth opportunities across defense and national security markets, state government programs, and technology-enabled services.

Maximus ( MMS ) expects adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 12.8% for fiscal year 2027 and adjusted diluted earnings per share to range between $7.50 and $8.00 per share.

This guidance assumes no incentive contribution related to the VA MDE contracts during fiscal year 2027. Fiscal year 2026 included incentive-related revenue and profit equal to an estimated $75 million and $1.05 adjusted earnings per share, respectively, total contribution across the first three quarters of the fiscal year 2026. Excluding the incentive contribution related to the VA MDE contracts to the fiscal year 2026, the midpoint of our adjusted diluted earnings per share guidance represents growth of approximately 8%.

We expect free cash flow to range between $700 million and $800 million. The outlook reflects DSO returning to the historical range of 60-70 days and includes the benefit of collections that shifted beyond fiscal year-end.

For fiscal year 2027, Maximus ( MMS ) expects amortization of intangible assets of approximately $96 million, depreciation and amortization of property, equipment and capitalized software of approximately $55 million, interest expense of approximately $110 million, an effective tax rate of approximately 25%, and weighted average shares outstanding of approximately 52.1 million.

Conference Call and Webcast Information

Maximus ( MMS ) will host a conference call today, November 19, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. ET.

The call is open to the public and available by webcast or by phone at:

As a leading strategic partner to government, Maximus ( MMS ) helps improve the delivery of public services amid complex technology, health, economic, and social challenges. data.title: Willis Lease Finance Corporation Expands Fleet with Acquisition of Two Airbus A320 Aircraft
data.description:
COCONUT CREEK, Fla., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Willis Lease Finance Corporation ( WLFC ) (the "Company"), the leading lessor of commercial aircraft engines and global provider of aviation services, today announces that it has completed the acquisition of two Airbus A320 aircraft.

The acquisitions complement the Company’s core engine leasing business and reflect its continued commitment to strategically expanding its aviation asset portfolio to meet growing customer demand.

“Demand for assets and flexible leasing solutions remains exceptionally strong in today’s environment,” said Austin C. Willis, President & Chief Executive Officer of Willis Lease Finance Corporation ( WLFC ). “We continue to grow our portfolio and strengthen our ability to serve airline customers around the world. The addition of both a new-generation A320neo and an A320ceo reflects our disciplined approach to investing in diverse assets.”

Willis Lease Finance Corporation ( WLFC )

Willis Lease Finance Corporation ( WLFC ) leases large and regional spare commercial aircraft engines and aircraft to airlines, aircraft engine manufacturers and maintenance, repair, and overhaul providers worldwide. These leasing activities are integrated with engine and aircraft trading, engine lease pools, and asset management services through Willis Mitsui & Co. Asset Management Limited, as well as various end-of-life solutions for engines and aviation materials provided through Willis Aeronautical Services, Inc. Through Willis Engine Repair Center®, Jet Centre by Willis, and Willis Aviation Services Limited, the Company’s service offerings include Part 145 engine maintenance, aircraft line and base maintenance, aircraft disassembly, parking and storage, airport FBO and ground and cargo handling services.

data.title: Anthropic's historic debut to put AI's promise and peril to Wall St test
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic's record $81 billion IPO brings to Wall Street an avatar of a sector that proponents herald as an economic panacea, while detractors warn it has stoked a market bubble and could ultimately threaten humanity itself.

More immediately, the Claude chatbot maker's debut after securing a $1.5 trillion valuation in the IPO, together with Tuesday's earnings report by AI poster child Nvidia ( NVDA ), signals the industry has nominally passed the two big tests facing it this week.

The strong demand for Anthropic shares amid a broader tech selloff offers hope to the sector, even as a rocky market reception for Nvidia ( NVDA ) results which looked strong at first blush, signals the euphoria around the sector has cooled.

"I've looked at this whole week as a referendum on AI. Nvidia ( NVDA ) gave us a read on the buildout, and Anthropic is about to give us a read on investor appetite for the next generation of AI companies," Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion, said before the Anthropic debut.

AI technology has boosted economic growth, sparked doomsday warnings and arguably helped usher in a data-center-skeptic Democratic tsunami in the US midterm elections.

Investors who once embraced the boom have turned skeptical in recent weeks over concerns that the enormous spending needed to build out the sector and the incipient crushing debt loads may not be justified by the eventual returns.

An extramarital-affair scandal involving Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO and a spike in Treasury yields have further unnerved investors.

AN INDUSTRY BENCHMARK

As the first frontier AI company to go public, Anthropic is poised to become the sector's benchmark, with its arch-rival OpenAI reportedly eyeing a 2027 listing.

The company sold 980 million shares at $83 each, pricing the IPO above its initial range of $70 to $78 set when it launched the roadshow. The additional $26 billion raised through a private placement takes the total haul to over $107 billion.

"Some of the demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out on the rare opportunity to gain exposure to a leading AI company, even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates passive demand from index-tracking funds will account for about 28% of Anthropic's shares offered, or roughly $19 billion.

When it debuts on the Nasdaq later on Thursday, Anthropic will join the world's trillion-dollar club, alongside technology giants such as Microsoft, Apple and Nvidia ( NVDA ).

The listing will also give retail investors a chance to pile into one of the AI industry's hottest names, potentially amplifying swings in the stock as trading begins.

The buzz has already spilled onto prediction markets, where traders are placing bets on everything from its opening pop to where the stock will close on its first day.

JUSTIFYING THE PRICE TAG

Debate has intensified across global markets in recent months over whether the AI boom is veering into bubble territory, with economists, some of the world's biggest CEOs, and political leaders split over its sustainability.

Much of the scrutiny has focused on circular financing arrangements. A complicated web of deals between AI companies, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors has raised questions over how much of the industry's growth is being fueled by money circulating within the same ecosystem.

Anthropic's breakneck growth has so far defied these concerns, but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying.

"It doesn't have to be a bad company for it to be a bad investment at the IPO price," said Nic Puckrin, cross-asset analyst and founder of Coin Bureau.

Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google, underscoring how its rapid growth hinges on securing vast amounts of future computing capacity, some of which relies on financing beyond the company's control.

Investors will be watching Anthropic's debut and subsequent trading closely, with analysts expecting the stock to emerge as a proxy for the broader AI trade as questions over valuations, spending and returns weigh on sentiment.

The company will also need to balance growth with calls to slow the development of advanced AI models over concerns that they pose cybersecurity threats and could be exploited by bad actors to target critical government and private infrastructure.

Anthropic warned in its IPO prospectus that AI could behave unpredictably and advance faster than oversight mechanisms, posing potentially "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity."

(Reporting by Niket Nishant, Manya Saini in Bengaluru and Echo Wang in New York; Additional reporting by Ragini Mathur; Editing by Christian Plumb and Arun Koyyur)
